## Source File Shape

A source file has an optional `module`, zero or more `import` declarations, and then any number of public declarations. The text grammar is the parser contract; normalized JSON is validated by `schema/lathe.schema.json` after defaults are inserted.

## Asset Declarations

Asset headers use `asset <name>: <kind>`, with optional `from <qident>` and `uses <qident>, ...` clauses before the body.

Supported asset kinds:

`hard_surface_prop`, `env_module`, `mechanical_assembly`

## Rules, Spaces, Tests, And Variants

- Validation-style rules use `ensure <expr>` and `prefer <expr> weight <number>`.
- Search spaces use `vary <path> in <expr>`, `freeze <path>`, `objective maximize|minimize <metric> weight <number>`, and `select best_of <number>`.
- Tests and benchmarks contain assignments plus `assert <expr>` statements.
- Variants use `set`, `append`, `remove`, and `unset` patches against dotted paths.

## Expressions And Literals

Identifiers match `[a-z][a-z0-9_]*`; qualified identifiers are dot-separated identifiers. Expressions support booleans, strings, numbers, unit literals, lists, calls, ranges, unary `not`/`-`, arithmetic, comparison, equality, `in`, `and`, and `or`.

Supported unit suffixes:

`mm`, `cm`, `m`, `deg`, `rad`, `g`, `kg`, `ms`, `s`, `kb`, `mb`, `gb`, `px`, `px_per_m`, `px_per_cm`
